review.canonical_rule: A date is archv_date iff it is the archivist's normalized cataloguing date in YEAR-FIRST "YYYY, Month [DD]" order (e.g. "1915, August 18", "1937, October") or a circa estimate ("c. 1944", "c. 1918 -"); it is typed, floats in the top corner (or, by FORM-IS-DISPOSITIVE, as a centered/right mid-page section divider between notebook years, e.g. "1934, January"), appears once per document (so >1 per multi-doc page), and NEVER connects. A date is src_date iff it is written by the source author in NATURAL order / numeric-shorthand / feast form — the letter's own dateline ("August 18th, 1915", "June 3, 1927", "Mar 27 1935", "3/8/57", "10 A.M. Dec. 27, 1927", "Christmas Day 1913"), the place-split right half of a mixed dateline, or a per-entry margin date in a notebook/journal column (left OR right margin: "Nov. 8th, 1923", "Oct. 13th", bare day numbers "17"/"26", partial-ditto explicit days "March 16" then "17"). When the same calendar date appears both top-corner (year-first) and in-text (natural order), top-corner=archv_date and in-text=src_date. Dates embedded inside an entry/body line (a saint's feast-year at the end of a list item, "Oct. 22-27-1939" inside a retreat-note title, a sentence-style "For December 1st 1937" heading at the body's own left margin) stay inside src_content and are NOT split out. A ditto/repeat mark is not a src_date and emits no polygon. The single sanctioned override: on a page that already carries a top-corner archv_date, a SECOND lower year-first date heading each per-enrollment Mass-card block stays src_date (rule 549 exception); such Mass-card src_dates never connect. The corpus follows this on ~73/75 pages essentially flawlessly.

review.tolerance_band: (1) Top-corner / mid-page-divider dates: STRICT — a date in year-first 'YYYY, Month [DD]' or circa form is archv_date with no defensible alternative; a date in natural / numeric / feast order that is the letter's own dateline or a notebook margin entry is src_date with no defensible alternative. A model must NOT be penalized for: calling any 'YYYY, Month DD' or 'c. YYYY' top/divider date archv_date, and calling any natural-order/numeric/feast dateline or left/right-margin per-entry notebook date src_date. (2) Mass-card per-card lower dates: BOTH readings defensible. On a multi-enrollment page that already has a top-corner archv_date, a lower per-card date that happens to be year-leading may be read EITHER as src_date (rule-549 exception; the corpus majority and the prescribed rule) OR as archv_date (the human did this on Appendix_3/page_019). Do not penalize a model for choosing src_date on such per-card dates (the rule-blessed answer), and do not penalize either choice as 'wrong' on the two equivalent pages. (3) Year-LEADING but non-comma source datelines ('1897 - Jan. 14th - 1947' jubilee spans on Volume_2/page_208, '1957 New Years' on Appendix_2/page_070): src_date is correct (author's own dateline text), but because they lead with a year they are borderline — do not penalize a model that, lacking the connection/role context, hesitates toward archv_date. (4) A feast word or embedded date INSIDE a notebook body line / entry title / body-margin sentence-heading ('For December 1st 1937', a list-item feast-year, 'Oct. 22-27-1939' in a title) stays in src_content; do not penalize a model for folding these into content rather than emitting src_date. (5) Mid-page year-first section dividers between notebook years ('1934, January', '1935, June' on Volume_3/page_218 and page_310; '1937, December' on Volume_4/page_006) are archv_date, NOT src_date — this is the clearest positive precedent and the correct counter to the Appendix_1/page_047 slip.

review.canonical_rule: Four structural marker types are kept distinct and are applied uniformly across the corpus: (1) struct_id = the document/source IDENTIFIER -- a notebook/catalog title-and-number ("FATHER SOLANUS NOTEBOOK NO. 11", "FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 3.") OR a centered, underlined piece-title on a formal document ("CAPUCHIN-FRANCISCAN APPRECIATION", "BAKED BEANS", "AUTOGRAPH TO MYSTICAL CITY OF GOD, VOL III / THE TRANSFIXION"); it sits high on the page (every instance y < 0.30*page_height), appears once per document, and NEVER connects. (2) struct_doc = a within-document, FAR-LEFT-margin page/section anchor ("Page 1", "Pg. 37.", "Page 217 Cont.", page ranges "Pgs. 33-36" / "Page 219 to 240", and retreat/outline markers "C.I."/"C.II."/"RETREAT"); every instance sits in the left margin (xL < 0.32*page_width) and is the dominant fan-out connection partner of src_content (and the rare archv_other<->struct_doc 'Blank/Page N' edge). (3) struct_other = a CONTINUATION-PAGE running header -- a reprinted RECIPIENT NAME directly above/below a 'Page N' marker ("Mrs. Margaret LeDoux"/"Mr. Charles Bracken"); never connects. (4) struct_commentary = an intra-document structural/layout note -- "On the reverse side... continues written by hand", "(Continued on the reverse of Card)", "Front"/"Back" photo side-labels, "Message written on the face of a photo."; never connects, and is distinguished from archv_commentary (provenance/transcription framing) and archv_other (terse page-status glosses). A geometry sweep of all 38 struct-bearing pages found 0 struct_id placed low and 0 struct_doc outside the left margin, confirming the rule holds with high consistency.

review.tolerance_band: struct_id vs struct_doc: defensible split is positional+role -- a title near the top naming the whole notebook/piece is struct_id; a left-margin per-page/per-section marker linked to a body block is struct_doc. A model should NOT be penalized either way for: (a) a centered underlined formal-letter piece-title being struct_id (canonical) -- this is firmly struct_id, not a tolerance case; (b) a 'Page N' header at the TOP of a formal continuous-prose letter that does NOT connect (Volume_1/page_200's bottom-corner '4.') being struct_doc-with-zero-edges -- accept as struct_doc whether or not a marker is drawn at all. struct_other vs struct_id/src_recipient on continuation pages: a reprinted RECIPIENT NAME running header above/below 'Page N' must be struct_other (never src_recipient); a reprinted TITLE running header is in the tolerance band between struct_other (running-header analogy, preferred) and struct_id (literal title text) -- do not penalize a model for choosing struct_other here even though the corpus instance used struct_id. struct_commentary: accept struct_commentary for genuine intra-document layout/transition notes ('On the reverse...', '(Continued on the reverse of Card)', 'Front'/'Back', 'Message written on the face of a photo.'); a medium-format descriptor like 'Photo of Fr. Solanus' is acceptably EITHER archv_format_note (corpus choice) or struct_commentary -- both defensible. Retreat/outline markers (C.I., RETREAT, I., A)) are struct_doc; tolerate src_other ONLY where the marker is fused on one physical line with adjacent dated text (as on Volume_1/245), but struct_doc is the canonical reading. Archivist page-range/end-of-notebook summary lines beside a struct_doc range marker may be EITHER archv_other (rule's literal example) or src_content (voice-tiebreaker if in the author's own summarizing voice); both connect to struct_doc, so the struct_doc label and its edge are correct regardless. Body section headings ('WANTED', verse numbers, '#608', '4)') are NOT struct_doc/struct_id and NOT 'other' -- they are src_content; no tolerance for promoting them to a structural/other category that creates a spurious connection.

review.canonical_rule: Letterhead splits into TWO regions by role: the sending institution/order NAME -> src_origin (kept whole in ONE box even across several stylized lines, including glue words "and"/"&" and a devotional "+"); the street, city, and state ADDRESS line(s) below the name -> a SEPARATE src_location_sender box (street + city/state may share one location box). When name and place are FUSED on one physical line, split it: institution -> src_origin (left), city/state/street -> src_location_sender (right). A bare city/state dateline with no institution ("Detroit, Michigan") is still src_location_sender, src_origin legitimately absent. Followed on ~15 of 20 letterhead pages (all Appendix_2 and Appendix_3 examples, plus Volume_1/082 fused-line, Volume_1/088, Volume_2/001, Volume_2/208, and bare-dateline Volume_2/084).
review.tolerance_band: A model should NOT be penalized for any of: (1) putting the street line and the city/state line in ONE src_location_sender box vs splitting them into two — the corpus keeps them together (Appendix_3/005, 007, 019; Volume_1/088) and never splits street from city, so the single combined box is canonical and the defensible reading. (2) Treating a fused single dateline line that begins with a place-like religious-house token but has NO "Monastery/Friary/Church" word and runs straight into city/state (Volume_2/347 "St. Felix, Huntington, Ind.") as ALL src_location_sender, OR splitting "St. Felix" off as src_origin — both defensible. (3) Origin appearing physically BELOW the signature or at the page bottom rather than at the top (Volume_2/001, Appendix_1/028, Appendix_1/031) — placement does not change the role. (4) On a bare dateline place with no institution name on its own line, emitting src_location_sender with NO src_origin (Volume_2/084). OUTSIDE tolerance (a real error): swallowing a clearly separate ADDRESS line (street or city/state on its own physical line below the name) inside the src_origin box; labeling a standalone institution-name line as src_content/other instead of src_origin; and fragmenting one multi-line institution NAME into multiple src_origin boxes.

Peace to Men.", "PAX ET BONUM!"; (4) a leading verse / epigraph / authored poem on a single-prose page stays INSIDE src_content (e.g. "HAIL Queen of the Heavens!", "Purpose of the Rational Creature ...", the "mourners' tear" stanza, the "Poor wanderers of a stormy day" verse). review.tolerance_band: A motto/blessing is correctly src_farewell whenever it sits on or above the signature after the body (including when it shares the closing line to the LEFT of the signature, or sits above a "[no signature]" slot). It is correctly src_greeting whenever a reader-addressed blessing opens the message above/at the salutation. A leading or set-apart authored verse/epigraph on a single-author continuous-prose page is correctly src_content. Solanus -", "Inside front cover.", "( On another sheet )". Solanus! Describes the rules and dues...", "There are just names and addresses for help wanted, etc."). archv_other is the ONLY archv_* that connects (rare archv_other<->struct_doc edge). (3) src_other = a SOURCE-document flourish that is not body/greeting/farewell/signature/date: an impersonal liturgical motto SET APART ('PRAISED BE JESUS CHRIST!'), a motto/doxology positioned BELOW the signature ('DEO GRATIAS', 'Praised be Jesus!', 'Praised Be The Most Blessed Sacrament!'), a Latin incipit ('IN NOMINE JESU INCIPIT A.D. 1911'), a care-of addressing line ('% Fr. O.K.'), a third-party Mass-card enrollment-attribution block ('special enrollment of Mrs. X by Daughter Doris'), and Mass-card membership-status tags ('Special Member', 'Emergency, special Membership'). review.canonical_rule: num_documents = the count of distinct CLOSED-then-OPENED messages on the page. A new document is incremented only when a strong cluster appears: (a) a NEW archivist provenance note ("The following is a faithful transcription...") and/or a new top-of-block archv_date header — the strongest signal; (b) a complete farewell+signature pair followed below by a NEW message, INCLUDING a later-DATED resumption block that carries ITS OWN signature (e.g. a "December 29th" continuation that is itself signed); (c) parallel self-contained recipient+date+body+signature units — N Seraphic Mass-card enrollments = N documents; (d) a 2x2 grid of parallel drafts — each quadrant a document. A block does NOT start a new document when it is: a P.S./postscript (even one bearing its OWN trailing signature), a "Page N"/"...Cont."/"Continued on the reverse" continuation (even with a reprinted recipient running header or a repeated greeting), an embedded poem/quotation/numbered list/recipe, or a new "Pg. N" notebook section. DECISIVE: an ENTIRE notebook / journal / ledger / retreat-notes page is exactly ONE document no matter how many "Pg. N" markers, margin dates, outline markers (C.I., I., A)) or itemized entries it holds. The pivotal distinction the corpus encodes: a separately-signed block that is a "P.S."/postscript stays the SAME document, whereas a separately-signed block introduced by a later DATE (a resumption) becomes a NEW document.

# Portable best-practices for a generalizable LLM document-layout LABELING workflow

Principles below are grounded in primary sources and mapped to your pipeline stages: **scheme design → few-shot curation → prompt → snap-to-ink → QA → human review.** Confidence is flagged where the literature disagrees.

---

## 1. Designing region/layout annotation SCHEMAS that minimize confusion and category overlap
*(maps to: scheme design; also constrains few-shot curation and QA)*

**P1.1 — Pick classes on four explicit axes, not intuition.** DocLayNet selected its 11 classes by weighing *(1) overall occurrence of the label, (2) specificity, (3) recognizability on a single page (no cross-page context needed), and (4) coverage of the page.* "**Specificity** ensures that the choice of label is not ambiguous, while **coverage** ensures that all meaningful items on a page can be annotated." Use these as a literal checklist when adding/merging a region class. *(DocLayNet, arXiv:2206.01062)*

**P1.2 — Make classes visually separable; avoid semantics-dependent labels.** DocLayNet deliberately "avoided class labels that are tightly linked to the semantics of the text… which goes beyond visual layout recognition." For layout, a category should be decidable from appearance/position alone. PubLayNet's own design rationale is the same: categories were chosen to "cover important document regions" (paragraph/title/list/image/table) that a vision model can learn distinctive patterns for. *(DocLayNet; PubLayNet, arXiv:1908.07836)*

**P1.3 — Expect irreducible ambiguity and write it down.** DocLayNet's annotation guideline is "**over 100 pages long**," full of positive/negative visual examples and explicit decision rules — yet they show cases where "criteria… can resolve cases A to C, while case D remains ambiguous." Takeaway: a long, example-driven, decision-tree-style guideline removes *most* overlap, but some residual ambiguity is structural — define a tie-breaking default rather than pretending it doesn't exist. *(DocLayNet)*

**P1.4 — Coverage vs. variability is a real tradeoff in scheme design.** PubLayNet is large but "severely lacks layout variability" (sourced only from PubMed/arXiv), so models trained on it "drop significantly… on more challenging and diverse layouts." If your scheme/examples come from one document type, expect poor transfer; diversify source documents per class. *(DocLayNet's comparison of PubLayNet)*

> **For your flow:** treat the labeling scheme as a versioned, example-rich guideline document (decision rules + canonical positive/negative crops per class), keep classes visually decidable on a single page, and record an explicit tie-break for the known "case-D" overlaps in your domain. These same canonical crops become your few-shot pool (§3).

---

## 2. MEASURING & HANDLING annotation INCONSISTENCY
*(maps to: QA, human review; gates which examples enter few-shot/training)*

### 2a. Which agreement metric to use

**P2.1 — Match the metric to the label type.**
- **Cohen's κ** — exactly 2 annotators, categorical; corrects for chance but requires both to label every item (impractical at scale).
- **Fleiss' κ** — 3+ annotators, fixed categories.
- **Krippendorff's α** — any number of annotators, **handles missing data and ordinal/interval scales**; the recommended default for production pipelines, and specifically proposed for vision because it "handles multiple raters, missed bounding boxes, and box-size variation."
*(Claru IAA glossary; Brenndoerfer IAA guide; "Assessing Data Quality… Krippendorff's Alpha for Computer Vision," arXiv:1912.10107)*

**P2.2 — Interpret κ/α with Landis & Koch bands:** `<0` poor · `0.01–0.20` slight · `0.21–0.40` fair · `0.41–0.60` moderate · `0.61–0.80` substantial · `0.81–1.00` almost perfect. A common production floor is **κ ≥ 0.70** for classification labels. *(Claru IAA glossary)*

**P2.3 — For spatial/box/region labels, kappa is the wrong tool; use overlap-based agreement.** Standard κ is "designed for categorical classification, not pixel-level spatial tasks," and suffers a **size bias**: when a region is small, background pixels dominate and "it is easy to achieve more than 50% overlap… [yet this] may not be… an acceptable inter-annotator agreement." Use **IoU/Jaccard (or Dice)** instead; combine with sensitivity/specificity and consensus methods (e.g., STAPLE) to avoid single-metric bias. Rough IoU bands: **0.75+ good, 0.85+ excellent.** *(Assessing IAA for Medical Image Segmentation, PMC10062409; Claru IAA glossary)*

**P2.4 — The field-standard agreement metric for document *layout* is mAP, not kappa.** DocLayNet computes inter-annotator agreement as **mAP@0.5–0.95 between pairwise annotations on triple-annotated pages** — this simultaneously captures *did they pick the same class* and *did they draw the same box*. This is the most directly transferable metric for your region-labeling task (it's exactly your detector's eval metric, so "human ceiling" and "model score" are comparable). *(DocLayNet)*

**P2.5 — Agreement is class- and domain-dependent; use it to find your weak classes.** DocLayNet's per-class triple-IAA (all domains): **Table 92–95%, List-item 87–88%, Section-header 86–88%, Caption 84–89%** — but the *per-domain* spread is huge, e.g., **Caption collapses to 40–61% on financial documents** while reaching 94–99% on scientific. **Models trail the human IAA ceiling by ~10%.** Practical rule: compute agreement *per class × per document-type*; the low cells are exactly where your guideline, your few-shot exemplars, and your human-review effort should concentrate. *(DocLayNet; per-class figures from the DocLayNet IAA tables)*

### 2b. Redundancy & adjudication protocol

**P2.6 — Redundantly annotate a subset, gate annotators, then adjudicate the disputes.** DocLayNet double-annotated 7,059 pages and triple-annotated 1,591, and **gated annotators through two qualifying exams (8 of 40 candidates failed the bar)** before production. General adjudication best-practice: keep a **10–15% overlap sample**, track **Krippendorff's α per annotator/day**, retrain or reassign anyone whose rolling α drops below threshold, and **route low-agreement items (e.g., α or confidence < 0.7) to an expert panel (2–3 reviewers)**; majority vote suits clear-cut classes, while expert sequential review suits hard/complex ones. **Dawid–Skene** can aggregate noisy annotators into a probabilistically weighted consensus label. *(DocLayNet; Encord "Achieving Annotation Consensus"; CleverX annotator-agreement guide; tagtog automatic adjudication)*

### 2c. EXCLUDE vs RELABEL noisy examples

**P2.7 — Find label errors automatically with Confident Learning / Cleanlab.** CL estimates the **joint distribution of noisy vs. true labels** using **per-class confidence thresholds = the average self-confidence (predicted prob.) of examples labeled with that class**, then ranks suspect items by mislabeling probability. It is **model-agnostic** (needs only predicted probabilities + noisy labels). Across 10 benchmark datasets it found an **average 3.4% label-error rate** (ImageNet val ~6%; QuickDraw ~10%), and human review confirmed **~51–54%** of algorithm-flagged candidates as genuine errors — cutting manual validation effort by up to ~90%. *(Confident Learning, arXiv:1911.00068 / JAIR; "Pervasive Label Errors," arXiv:2103.14749; Northcutt blog)*

**P2.8 — Off-diagonal mass = class overlap. Use it to fix your *scheme*, not just your data.** Because off-diagonal entries in the confident joint mean "the noisy class and true class must be different," large off-diagonals reveal **ontological overlap between two of your classes** (CL surfaced relationships like "bathtub is a tub" in ImageNet). If two of your region classes trade mass heavily, that's a §1 scheme problem — merge them or sharpen the guideline. *(Confident Learning; Northcutt blog)*

**P2.9 — Default to PRUNE (exclude) for training data; CORRECT (relabel) for evaluation data.** This is the one place sources look contradictory but actually aren't — the action depends on the data's role:
- **Training set → prune.** CL "follow[s] the principle of pruning noisy data (as opposed to fixing label errors)"; empirically, "**100% pruning got the highest accuracy, while relabelling all got the worst**," and accuracy "starts to go down linearly" as you relabel more — because *automatic* relabeling injects new errors. Remove suspect examples (or down-weight them) rather than auto-correcting. *(Northcutt blog; Suneeta Mall / TDS analysis; Cleanlab GSoC study)*
- **Test/eval set → correct, don't drop.** Pervasive-Label-Errors advises practitioners to "**correct your test set labels**" — because errors there silently **flip model rankings**: on ImageNet, **ResNet-18 beats ResNet-50 once mislabeled-test prevalence rises just ~6%** (VGG-11 > VGG-19 at +5% on CIFAR-10). Dropping examples changes the distribution you measure on; correcting preserves it. *(Pervasive Label Errors, arXiv:2103.14749)*
- **Either way, human-confirm before acting:** CL flags candidates, but "**it is best to go through the examples… and decide whether to remove or relabel**." *(Northcutt blog)*

> **For your flow:** report agreement as **mAP@[.5:.95] (boxes) + per-class κ/α (class choice)** on a redundantly-labeled subset; run Cleanlab over your auto-labeler's confidences to triage suspects; **prune/quarantine** noisy items from the *few-shot pool and any training set*, but **adjudicate-and-correct** items in your held-out *evaluation* set; treat heavy cross-class confusion as a signal to revise the scheme (§1).

---

## 3. CURATING FEW-SHOT examples so contradictory demonstrations don't degrade the LLM
*(maps to: few-shot curation; directly downstream of §2 quality gates)*

**P3.1 — Do NOT rely on the "labels don't matter" result.** Min et al. 2022 famously showed that **replacing gold labels with random labels "barely hurts" performance** on classification/multiple-choice across 12 models, arguing demonstrations mainly convey **(a) the label space, (b) the input distribution, and (c) the format**. This is widely over-applied. *(Min et al., "Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations," EMNLP 2022, arXiv:2202.12837)*

**P3.2 — In practice, exemplar correctness DOES matter — often a lot — so curate clean exemplars.** Direct rebuttals quantify it:
- **"Ground-Truth Labels Matter" (Yoo et al., EMNLP 2022):** the gap between correct-label and fully-incorrect-label demos was **as large as ~80% accuracy** on some tasks (hate-speech, GPT-J); per-task **Label-Correctness Sensitivity ranged up to 0.815**. Macro-averaging (as in Min et al.) *hides* this. *(arXiv:2205.12685)*
- **Noise degrades both accuracy and stability:** as demonstration label-noise rises, ICL accuracy drops sharply (e.g., **46.9%→31.8%** at 50% noise, SST-5) and **prediction variance increases**. *(In-Context Learning with Noisy Labels, arXiv:2411.19581)*
- **Generation ≠ classification:** for *generation/extraction* tasks (closer to your structured-label output), "**label noise in the demonstrations significantly degrades ICL's performance… different from previous results on classification**," and **adding more demonstrations does not bridge the gap.** Since your layout-labeling output is structured generation, treat exemplar correctness as critical. *(On the Noise Robustness of ICL for Text Generation, arXiv:2405.17264)*

**P3.3 — Curate for *consistency*, not just correctness.** Contradictory demonstrations (two near-identical inputs labeled differently — exactly what inter-annotator disagreement produces) are the worst case: noisy demos "interfere with [the] learning process," and selection methods can even attach a wrong-label demo to a semantically similar test input, propagating the error. So the few-shot pool must be **internally non-contradictory** — run §2's agreement/CL checks on candidate exemplars and exclude disputed ones. *(arXiv:2411.19581; "Learn to Select," arXiv:2511.10675)*

**P3.4 — Control selection and ordering; they swing results by tens of points.** ICL is "highly sensitive to which demonstrations are included," and the gap between the best and worst **ordering can reach ~30%**. Fix a **deterministic default ordering** for a chosen exemplar set and select exemplars deliberately (e.g., similarity/coverage-based) rather than at random. *(Order/positional-bias literature, arXiv:2402.15637, arXiv:2507.22887; selection sensitivity per Min et al. and follow-ups)*

**P3.5 — Mitigations that survive some noise.** If you can't fully clean the pool: **verbose/explanatory prompt templates lower label-correctness sensitivity** (0.189–0.308) without hurting accuracy, and **demonstration "rectification"** (a small model that rewrites noisy demo labels to corrected ones) restores accuracy *and* cuts variance (σ 1.98→0.83 on MRPC). *(Ground-Truth Labels Matter, arXiv:2205.12685; ICL with Noisy Labels, arXiv:2411.19581)*

> **For your flow:** the few-shot pool should be your **highest-agreement, adjudicated, mutually-consistent** crops (the clean output of §2). Pin exemplar **order**, select by **similarity/coverage** to the target page, prefer **verbose rule-bearing prompts**, and **quarantine any exemplar that §2 flagged as disputed** — for structured/extraction output, wrong exemplars hurt more than the classification literature implies.

## 4. RECALL / COVERAGE for detection/extraction WITHOUT overfitting
*(maps to: prompt + snap-to-ink + QA; second-pass review)*

**P4.1 — Sample multiple times and aggregate (self-consistency).** Sample N reasoning paths at modest temperature and take the **majority/mode**; this "marginalizes over reasoning paths" and yields **~9–15% absolute accuracy gains over greedy single-pass decoding.** Practical recipe (Instructor docs): temperature ≈ 0.5, ~5 samples, vote with a counter. *(Wang et al., "Self-Consistency…", arXiv:2203.11171; Instructor self-consistency docs)*

**P4.2 — For structured/free-form outputs, exact-match voting breaks — use Universal Self-Consistency.** When outputs are boxes/structured records (no single canonical string to vote on), have **a second LLM pass judge which candidate is most consistent** with the rest, rather than naive string voting. *(Universal Self-Consistency; Instructor docs)*

**P4.3 — Add a second-pass SELF-VERIFICATION stage to gain precision cheaply.** Verification exploits an **asymmetry: checking an extraction is easier than producing it.** A generate-then-verify pipeline (the model re-reads each candidate and asks "is this actually supported / is this really an X?") **consistently improves accuracy across LLMs** and is the documented fix for LLMs "over-confidently label[ing] NULL inputs as entities" (false positives). It also yields **provenance as short text spans**, which makes human audit fast. *(Self-Verification Improves Few-Shot Clinical IE, arXiv:2306.00024; GPT-NER self-verification, arXiv:2304.10428)*

**P4.4 — Name the recall↔precision tradeoff and choose per stage.** Verification "particularly strengthens precision (reducing false positives)… may slightly reduce recall." Comparative results: "**conservative verification achieves best precision at the expense of recall, while hierarchical-consistency methods find a nice trade-off.**" So: drive **recall in pass 1** (permissive prompt + multi-sample union of candidates), then drive **precision in pass 2** (verification/voting to filter). Don't ask a single pass to do both. *(Self-Verification IE, arXiv:2306.00024; VeriFY/self-consistency comparisons)*

**P4.5 — Recover recall via *union of samples*, not by loosening one prompt.** Because self-consistency samples diverse paths, the **union of detected regions across N samples raises coverage** of rare/edge regions, while §4.3 verification removes the spurious extras — increasing recall without the precision collapse that a single over-permissive prompt causes. *(self-consistency rationale, arXiv:2203.11171; verification filter, arXiv:2306.00024)*

**P4.6 — Avoid overfitting to the few-shot exemplars (anti-overfit).** Concrete guards from the cited literature:
- **Diversify exemplar sources** so the model doesn't learn one document type's quirks (PubLayNet's single-source brittleness, §P1.4). *(DocLayNet/PubLayNet)*
- **Resist ordering/selection memorization:** rotate/standardize order and select by similarity-to-target so the model conditions on *relevant* structure, not a fixed sequence it overfits to (§P3.4). *(order-sensitivity papers)*
- **Verify against the *input*, not the exemplars:** P4.3's grounding ("is this span actually in *this* page?") forces evidence from the target document rather than pattern-matching the demos — the key mechanism that curbs exemplar overfitting and hallucinated regions. *(Self-Verification IE; GPT-NER)*
- **Keep the held-out eval set CORRECTED and unseen** (§P2.9) so you can detect overfitting/regression honestly — the Pervasive-Label-Errors ranking-flip result shows a noisy eval set will mislead you about which prompt/config is actually better. *(Pervasive Label Errors)*

> **For your flow:** make pass 1 a **high-recall, multi-sample** layout detection (union of candidates), run **snap-to-ink**, then a **pass-2 self-verification** ("is each region really class X, and is its box tight to the ink?") plus **universal self-consistency** voting for the final set; report precision/recall separately, and guard overfitting with diverse exemplars, standardized ordering, input-grounded verification, and a corrected held-out eval set.

acceptable_ranges.rule: Four distinct types: (1) struct_id = the document/source IDENTIFIER (notebook title-and-number, or a centered underlined formal piece-title); sits high (y<0.30*H), once per document, NEVER connects. (2) struct_doc = a within-document FAR-LEFT-margin page/section anchor ('Page 1','Pg. 37','Pgs. 33-36', outline markers 'C.I.'/'RETREAT'); always xL<0.32*W; dominant fan-out partner of src_content. (3) struct_other = a continuation-page running header (reprinted RECIPIENT NAME above/below 'Page N'); never connects. (4) struct_commentary = an intra-document layout/transition note ('On the reverse...','Front'/'Back'); never connects. Body section sub-headings ('WANTED', verse numbers, '#608') stay src_content.
acceptable_ranges.tolerance: struct_id vs struct_doc is positional+role: centered top piece-title naming the whole notebook/piece = struct_id (firm, not a tolerance case); left-margin per-page marker linked to a body block = struct_doc. ACCEPT EITHER: a reprinted TITLE running header on a continuation page as struct_other (running-header analogy, preferred) OR struct_id (literal title text; the corpus instance on Volume_2/page_136); a 'Page N' header at the top of a formal letter that does not connect as struct_doc-with-zero-edges regardless of whether a marker is drawn; an outline marker fused on ONE physical line with adjacent dated text ('Tuesday - C.I.' on Volume_1/page_245) as src_other, though struct_doc is canonical; a medium-format descriptor ('Photo of Fr. Solanus') as archv_format_note OR struct_commentary. NO TOLERANCE for promoting a body section heading ('WANTED') to 'other' or a structural category (it creates a spurious edge); reprinted RECIPIENT name = struct_other, never src_recipient or 'other'.

acceptable_ranges.rule: Letterhead splits by role: sending institution/order NAME -> src_origin (kept WHOLE in ONE box across stylized lines incl. glue words 'and'/'&' and devotional '+'); the street/city/state ADDRESS line(s) below the name -> a SEPARATE src_location_sender box (street + city/state may share one location box). Name+place FUSED on one physical line: split institution left -> src_origin, city/state/street right -> src_location_sender. A bare city/state dateline with no institution ('Detroit, Michigan') is src_location_sender, src_origin legitimately absent. src_origin position is irrelevant (top, foot, or embedded mid-card all valid).
acceptable_ranges.tolerance: ACCEPT EITHER: street line + city/state line in ONE src_location_sender box (canonical) vs split into two; a fused single dateline beginning with a place-like religious-house token lacking a 'Monastery/Friary/Church' word ('St. Felix, Huntington, Ind.' on Volume_2/page_347) as ALL src_location_sender OR splitting 'St. Felix' off as src_origin; src_origin appearing physically below the signature or page-bottom; a bare dateline place -> src_location_sender with NO src_origin. OUTSIDE TOLERANCE (true error): swallowing a separate ADDRESS line (street or city/state on its own physical line below the name) inside src_origin; labeling a standalone institution-name line as src_content/other instead of src_origin; fragmenting one multi-line institution NAME into multiple src_origin boxes.

acceptable_ranges.rule: src_origin = the SENDING institution's letterhead/identity line(s); src_signature = the AUTHOR's personal sign-off NAME + order suffix ('Fr. Solanus, O.F.M.Cap.','Fr. Sol.'), always preceded by a separate src_farewell valediction. The distinction is by CONTENT/role (institution identity vs personal name), NOT page position: a reproduced letterhead is src_origin even at the foot of, or embedded inside, a Mass-card/Jubilee-card transcription.
acceptable_ranges.tolerance: On THIS axis the corpus is clean — zero swaps. ACCEPT EITHER on the adjacent origin/location cut (folding a place line into src_origin vs peeling it) and on position/segmentation variants. OUTSIDE TOLERANCE (penalize; none observed): tagging a personal 'Fr. Solanus'/'Fr. Sol.' sign-off as src_origin; tagging an institutional letterhead as src_signature; merging the farewell valediction or the name+suffix into src_origin instead of src_farewell/src_signature.

acceptable_ranges.rule: Liturgical mottos/doxologies/blessings labeled by POSITION relative to body and signature: (1) ON or ABOVE the signature after the body = src_farewell; (2) BELOW or to the RIGHT of (after) the signature name = src_other; (3) OPENING the message above/at the salutation, reader-addressed = src_greeting; (4) a leading verse/epigraph/authored poem set apart on a single-prose page stays INSIDE src_content. Below-signature->src_other and above-signature->src_farewell are the most reliable halves; the opening greeting-vs-other boundary is the fuzziest.
acceptable_ranges.tolerance: DEFENSIBLE-EITHER-WAY zones (do not penalize): (a) a motto SHARING the exact sign-off line to the LEFT of the signature may be src_farewell (position) OR src_other (habitual impersonal sign-off motto) — both in the gold set for 'Praised be Jesus Christ. | Fr. Sol.' (page_028 farewell vs page_031 other); (b) an OPENING doxology above its OWN dateline+salutation may be src_greeting OR src_other — the deciding factor is an intervening separate dateline (the rule never states this — a genuine prompt-gap; gold uses both for 'Blessed be God in all His designs!'); (c) an impersonal opening canticle/Latin tag may be src_greeting or src_other depending on the intervening dateline. NOT in zone (a): a closing doxology on its OWN line ABOVE the signature (not sharing the line) is unambiguously src_farewell — do not over-extend (a) to own-line-above-signature closings (Appendix_1/page_045).

acceptable_ranges.rule: Inside-address three-way split: (1) addressee NAME line = src_recipient (may carry leading 'To' and/or trailing colon/period); (2) recipient city/convent/street line(s) directly below the name = src_location_recipient (multi-line = ONE box); (3) opening salutation ('My Dear Sister Margaret:-') = src_greeting. A name embedded INSIDE the salutation stays src_greeting (not peeled). A recipient name reprinted as a continuation running header above/below 'Page N' = struct_other. A letter may carry MULTIPLE src_greeting polygons (opening doxology + personal salutation). On Mass-enrollment cards there is normally NO src_greeting: addressee NAME = src_recipient; the intention/dedication tag, 'God bless you <name>' well-wish, feast words, closing blessing = src_content; sign-off = src_signature.
acceptable_ranges.tolerance: ACCEPT EITHER: a pure name/title line as src_recipient even with leading 'To'/trailing colon vs src_greeting only when it begins 'Dear/My Dear ...:'; for a 'Dear <name>:-' line with NO separate name line, src_greeting is canonical and src_recipient is the ERROR (Appendix_1/page_028,031); a name fused into the salutation kept inside src_greeting (splitting a separate src_recipient acceptable only if the name truly sits on its own physical line); one or two separate opening-doxology+salutation greeting polygons. POSITION DECIDES for 'God bless you <name>': above/at the salutation = src_greeting; as the FIRST BODY sentence after an existing salutation = src_content. NORMATIVE: the Mass-card intention/dedication tag = src_content; labeling it src_greeting (Volume_2/page_075 doc_1, Appendix_1/page_042 doc_2) or 'other' (Appendix_3/page_019) is the outlier scored as src_content.

acceptable_ranges.rule: Role/position hierarchy; the SPECIFIC category almost always wins over the catch-all. (1) archv_other = terse archivist status/gloss in modern third-person voice. (2) struct_other = a recipient/addressee name REPRINTED as a running header above/below 'Page N'. (3) src_other = a SOURCE-document flourish not body/greeting/farewell/signature/date (impersonal motto set apart or below the signature, Latin incipit, care-of line, set-apart Scripture epigraph heading a sub-document, dated marginal author remark, third-party enrollment-attribution block, Mass-card membership-status tag). (4) other = role-neutral leftover belonging to NEITHER author NOR archivist, reserved for pre-printed Mass-card boilerplate ('has been enrolled in the Mass Association') or stray proofing marks; meant to be extremely rare. Decisive: 'other' is a last resort — author text -> src_*, archivist text -> archv_*/struct_*.
acceptable_ranges.tolerance: ACCEPT within range: (1) Mass-card intention/dedication phrase = src_content (canonical) OR src_other (set-apart top-of-card banner) OR src_greeting (only when fused into the salutation/recipient box) — 'other' NOT defensible. (2) doxology/motto near the sign-off = {src_farewell on/above the signature, src_other below it or impersonal}; opening set-apart doxology = {src_greeting, src_other}. (3) notebook/section banner headings ('WANTED','NOTES- Perhaps 1 out of Fifty','RETREAT') = src_other preferred; 'other' tolerated ONLY because the corpus itself uses it on two such banners (do not hard-fail), but src_other is preferred. OUTSIDE TOLERANCE: reprinted recipient running header over 'Page N' must be struct_other (src_recipient/'other' WRONG); 'Original in possession of:' block must be archv_possessor (archv_other WRONG); archv_other status/gloss notes have NO tolerance to src_content/struct_commentary. acceptable_ranges.rule: PAGE TYPE governs connections. (A) NOTEBOOK/JOURNAL/LEDGER/retreat-outline/index pages: left-margin struct_doc page/section markers and left/right-margin per-entry src_date dates fan out to body src_content blocks; a single Page-N marker links to EVERY content block in its vertical span (terminated only by the next Page-N marker, never by an intervening date); a content block routinely carries TWO edges (its struct_doc marker AND its margin src_date). (B) FORMAL LETTERS and a continuation 'Page N' header at the TOP of a letter: ZERO edges. (C) MASS-ENROLLMENT/SMA cards and Golden-Jubilee-card drafts: ZERO edges even when several cards share a page. Only 5 undirected pairs ever appear: src_content<->struct_doc, src_content<->src_date, archv_other<->struct_doc, archv_format_note<->src_content, other<->struct_doc. Manifest 'edges' counts DIRECTED entries (= 2x undirected).
acceptable_ranges.tolerance: EDGE PRESENCE is NOT ambiguous and shows ZERO genuine inconsistencies — PENALIZE: emitting ANY edge on a formal letter, a 'Page N' continuation header, a Mass/enrollment card, or a Jubilee-card draft; any pair outside the 5 allowed; linking src_date to anything but src_content, or struct_doc to src_date/archv_date; cross-document edges; or, on a genuine notebook, dropping a Page-N fan-out edge. ACCEPT (count/label nuance, not edge-presence): undirected vs doubled-directed edge totals; a top-corner natural-order date duplicating the archv_date called src_date-unlinked OR archv_date (edgeless either way); a full-width section-heading line beginning 'Pg. N' given its own edgeless struct_doc box in addition to the left-margin marker, provided the left-margin marker carries the fan-out (Appendix_2/page_006); exact src_content polygon granularity within one date/Page span; index/contents pages via src_content<->struct_doc (canonical).
